rationale: This quasi-experimental study uses municipal panel difference-in-differences models (with municipality and year fixed effects and propensity-score common-support trimming) across Colombian municipalities (1990-2005) to evaluate the 1994 Law 142 utility reforms enacted within Colombia's 1990s municipal decentralization framework. The central empirical exposure (regulatory_model_ownership) compares corporatized specialized providers (government-owned EICEs and public, mixed, or private ESP S.A. utility corporations, including interactions for private/mixed capital participation) against continued direct municipal provision, while decentralization (institutional_structure_coordination) forms the enabling institutional background allowing local governments to choose whether to reform. Alongside child mortality, the water/sanitation access outcome empirically estimated is municipal household water supply and sewerage coverage from the 1993 and 2005 censuses (primary_connection).
